metadata.title: Papyrus System Security Plan
metadata.remarks: This is an OSCAL System Security Plan (SSP) template for Papyrus, a bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC), air-gapped-first product. The primary deployment model is customer-owned-and-operated: the customer deploys Papyrus inside its own authorization boundary and owns the infrastructure, boundary, and authorization. Beag Labs provides software and documentation only — it does not host, operate, or control any production deployment, and receives no telemetry or operational data. Air-gapped and disconnected deployments (IL4/IL6, classified networks) are first-class profiles. Cloud-capable operation (commercial profile on customer-managed cloud) is a supported secondary option. This SSP is auto-generated from the Papyrus OSCAL Component Definition (v0.2.0) and describes the system boundary, characteristics, and selected NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 control implementations. It is NOT an authorization, certification, assessment result, or assertion that any deployment satisfies the referenced controls. A deploying customer must tailor system characteristics (FIPS 199 categorization, authorization boundary, environment), instantiate components inside the actual boundary, supply inherited controls, attach evidence, and assess effectiveness within its own authorization boundary.

system-characteristics.description: Papyrus is a bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC), air-gapped-first multiplayer product-development canvas for regulated and disconnected environments. The primary deployment model is customer-owned-and-operated: the customer deploys Papyrus inside its own authorization boundary (bare-metal, VM, container, or customer-controlled cloud account) and owns the boundary, infrastructure, and authorization. There is no Beag Labs multi-tenant control plane; each agency or security boundary runs an independent authoritative Papyrus service with local SQLite storage. Air-gapped and disconnected deployments (IL4/IL6, classified networks) are first-class profiles, not degraded modes. Cloud-capable operation (commercial profile on customer-managed AWS/Azure/GCP) is supported as a secondary option for regulated-but-connected environments. An authoritative Papyrus service and SQLite database run per agency or security boundary. Authenticated browsers collaborate through server-sequenced WebSocket operations. Typed directed-graph product artifacts remain connected. Human-reviewed AI persona agents and skills operate against the same authoritative project state. Profile-gated operation (PAPYRUS_PROFILE) constrains authentication methods, model endpoint access, agent availability, and cross-domain export behavior across commercial, NIPRNet/IL4, and SIPRNet/IL6 deployment modes.

authorization-boundary.description: PRIMARY (air-gapped / BYOC): The authorization boundary is entirely customer-owned and customer-operated. It encompasses the authoritative Papyrus service process (papyrus serve), its SQLite database and operation log, the deployed browser application, the agent and skill runtime, and the configured model endpoint client — all running inside the customer's authorization boundary on customer-owned or customer-controlled infrastructure (bare-metal, VM, container, or customer-controlled cloud account). Beag Labs provides software and a component definition; it does not operate, host, or control any part of the production boundary. There is no shared multi-tenant control plane, no Beag Labs managed service, and no data flows to Beag Labs infrastructure in the primary deployment model. Inherited controls (host OS, storage encryption, network enclave, CDS, physical/environmental) are supplied by the customer's own infrastructure or cloud provider authorization — not by Beag Labs. SECONDARY (cloud-capable BYOC): For regulated-but-connected commercial deployments, the customer may deploy Papyrus inside its own cloud account (AWS, Azure, GCP, or GovCloud). In this mode the customer's cloud provider may supply additional inherited controls (PE, CM-8, CP, SC-28) via the provider's own FedRAMP authorization, but the authorization boundary remains customer-owned — Beag Labs still does not host or control the deployment. Regardless of mode, each agency or security boundary runs its own authoritative service with local SQLite storage; there is no shared state, no cross-deployment data sync, and no Beag Labs operational access to production systems.
authorization-boundary.remarks: Customer must tailor this boundary description to the actual deployment. For air-gapped deployments (IL4/IL6, classified networks), document the enclave, host hardware, storage media, and CDS. For cloud-capable deployments (commercial profile), document the cloud account, VPC, subnets, leveraged cloud provider authorization, and any inherited controls.

network-architecture.description: Air-gapped primary: The Papyrus service runs enclave-local with no public internet connectivity. Authenticated browser clients connect over enclave-local HTTPS (REST) and WebSocket. No public discovery, STUN, TURN, relay, or outbound internet calls are required. Model inference uses a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint inside the enclave (IL6) or an approved enclave endpoint (IL4). Updates and cross-domain transfer use signed bundles verified against trusted deployment identities and processed through the customer's approved CDS. Cloud-capable secondary (commercial profile): The Papyrus service runs in the customer's own cloud account (VPC/subnet). Authenticated browser clients connect over HTTPS and WebSocket through customer-controlled TLS termination, load balancers, and security groups. The service may call a customer-configured model endpoint (Cloudflare Workers AI or customer-managed OpenAI-compatible inference). The customer provisions and controls all cloud networking, firewalls, IAM, and segmentation; Beag Labs has no network access to the deployment. The Papyrus CLI connects to the same authoritative service for administrative operations in both modes.
network-architecture.remarks: Customer must document the actual network diagram, ports, firewall rules, and segmentation. For air-gapped deployments, document enclave topology and CDS. For cloud deployments, document VPC topology, security groups, and cloud-provider network controls.

data-flow.description: Air-gapped primary data flows: 1) Browser to Papyrus service: authenticated REST and WebSocket over enclave-local TLS. 2) Papyrus service to SQLite: local file I/O for project state, operation log, audit, credentials, and configuration — all on enclave-local storage. 3) Papyrus service to model endpoint: inference calls to a self-hosted or enclave-approved OpenAI-compatible endpoint (no internet egress). 4) Papyrus service to IdP: authentication handshakes (CAC/PIV certificate validation, WebAuthn origin check). 5) Cross-domain transfer: signed bundles between explicitly trusted deployment identities, subject to the customer's approved CDS process. 6) Updates: signed bundle-based updates imported via the customer's approved media or CDS. NO data flows to Beag Labs infrastructure in the primary model. Cloud-capable secondary data flows (commercial profile only): flows 1-2 are identical; flow 3 may call a customer-configured external model endpoint over customer-controlled HTTPS; flow 4 adds OIDC/SAML federation. Beag Labs receives no telemetry, analytics, or operational data in either mode.
data-flow.remarks: Customer must attach or reference a data flow diagram and list all external dependencies. For air-gapped deployments, confirm zero egress. For cloud deployments, document any model endpoint egress.

components.title: Papyrus
components.description: A self-hosted, multiplayer product-development canvas for regulated and disconnected environments, with profile-gated identity, authoritative server-sequenced collaboration, locally persisted SQLite project data and operations, auditable agent and skill execution, and human-reviewed AI assistance.
components.purpose: Provide a self-hosted collaboration and product-development component that can contribute security mechanisms and evidence to a customer-owned authorization boundary.

components.title: Host Operating System / Container Runtime
components.description: Customer-managed host operating system and/or container runtime on which the Papyrus service process executes.

components.title: Identity Provider (IdP)
components.description: Customer-managed identity provider (CAC/PIV infrastructure, WebAuthn authenticators, OIDC provider, or SAML IdP). The IdP is authoritative for identity proofing, lifecycle, recovery, and revocation.

components.title: Model Inference Endpoint
components.description: Customer-configured model inference endpoint (Cloudflare Workers AI or OpenAI-compatible service). Disabled or enclave-local in IL4/IL6 profiles.

components.title: Network / Enclave / Monitoring Platform
components.description: Customer-managed network segmentation, firewall, TLS termination, SIEM/monitoring, backup, and storage encryption infrastructure.

control-implementation.description: Implementation of selected NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 controls. Each implemented-requirement references the Papyrus component (65d5f633) via by-component statements, plus inherited/shared customer components where applicable. Responsibility and implementation-status properties are carried over from the Papyrus Component Definition (v0.2.0).

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus provides project membership, organization membership, invitation, credential, and role records. Deploying organizations remain responsible for identity proofing, account approval, periodic review, disablement policy, and upstream identity-provider lifecycle management.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: The Papyrus service maintains organization membership, project membership, role assignments, invitation records, and credential enrollment/removal records. External identity binding is recorded with provenance.

implementation-status.remarks: Customer must supply identity proofing, account approval workflow, periodic review, and IdP lifecycle.

implemented-requirements.description: The daemon enforces authenticated sessions and project-scoped RBAC before protected operations. REST and WebSocket operations are evaluated against the caller identity and assigned project permissions.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: All REST and WebSocket operations require an authenticated session. The service evaluates each request against the caller's organization membership and project role before permitting protected operations.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus exposes role-based project permissions and separates ordinary member actions from administrative operations. Customers define role assignments, privileged administrators, and separation-of-duties policy.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Papyrus separates member-level actions from organization/project administrative operations through role assignments and permission checks.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus applies request rate limits to authentication-sensitive endpoints and rejects invalid challenges and credentials. Customers configure upstream IdP, reverse-proxy, and enclave account-lockout thresholds.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: The service rate-limits authentication endpoints and rejects invalid WebAuthn challenges, OIDC tokens, SAML assertions, and credentials.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus issues bounded sessions and supports explicit logout and credential revocation workflows. Deployment owners set session lifetime, inactivity, and emergency termination requirements.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Sessions are bounded and the service supports explicit logout and credential revocation.

implemented-requirements.description: Profile-gated authentication supports CAC/PIV for SIPRNet/IL6, CAC/PIV and WebAuthn for NIPRNet/IL4, and WebAuthn, OIDC, or SAML for commercial deployments. Authentication strength depends on customer-selected providers and configuration.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: PAPYRUS_PROFILE gates available authenticators: CAC/PIV (IL6), CAC/PIV+WebAuthn (IL4), WebAuthn/OIDC/SAML (commercial). External identities are bound to Papyrus member keys.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus binds an externally authenticated identity to a locally generated member public key and records provenance for the binding. Customers remain authoritative for enterprise identifiers and reassignment policy.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Papyrus generates member public keys and binds externally authenticated identities with provenance records. Identifier uniqueness and reassignment are governed by customer enterprise identity.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus supports WebAuthn credential enrollment and removal, CAC/PIV certificate validation, OIDC key discovery, and SAML IdP certificates. Customers control certificate issuance, trust anchors, provider keys, recovery, rotation, and revocation.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: WebAuthn enrollment/removal, CAC/PIV validation, OIDC discovery, and SAML certificate validation are handled by the service. Trust anchors, issuance, recovery, and rotation are customer-managed.

implemented-requirements.description: Commercial deployments may federate external identities through OIDC or SAML. The customer determines whether non-organizational access is permitted and configures federation claims, assurance requirements, and sponsorship.

e2c1a3b4-3001-4000-8000-000000000031.description: External user federation and assurance is configured by the customer via OIDC/SAML providers.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus defines security-relevant audit events for authentication, membership, role changes, project lifecycle, canvas mutation, agent and skill execution, export, configuration, and integrity verification.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: The service defines and emits auditable events for authentication, membership, roles, project lifecycle, canvas operations, agent/skill execution, export, configuration, and integrity verification.

implemented-requirements.description: Audit records identify time, actor, action, target, outcome, project context, and integrity-chain data where applicable. Secrets, raw authenticators, private keys, and bearer tokens are excluded from normal audit content.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Audit records include time, actor, action, target, outcome, project context, and hash-chain data. Secrets and raw authenticators are excluded.

props.name: control-title
props.value: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting

implemented-requirements.description: Authorized users can retrieve and review project audit history and verify the audit chain. Customers establish review cadence, alert rules, escalation paths, and correlation with enclave monitoring systems.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Authorized users can retrieve project audit history and verify the audit integrity chain within the service.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus records ISO 8601 timestamps from the host operating system. Accurate, synchronized, and authoritative time is inherited from the deployment platform and must be configured by the customer.

e2c1a3b4-3000-4000-8000-000000000030.description: The host OS provides authoritative, synchronized time. Papyrus records ISO 8601 timestamps from the platform clock.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus uses append-oriented, hash-linked audit records to make modification detectable. Customers protect database files, exports, backups, host access, and external log destinations.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Audit records are append-oriented and hash-linked so tampering is detectable.

implemented-requirements.description: The daemon generates audit records at server-side enforcement points for supported security and business operations, allowing consistent collection regardless of client interface.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Audit records are generated at server-side enforcement points for all supported security and business operations.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus provides profile-driven defaults for commercial, NIPRNet/IL4, and SIPRNet/IL6 modes. Customers document the approved deployment manifest, operating system, container, network, IdP, model endpoint, service binding, and storage configuration.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: PAPYRUS_PROFILE provides deterministic baseline defaults for authentication, model access, connectivity, agents, and export.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus configuration is file- and environment-driven and can be version controlled. Approval, testing, deployment, rollback, and emergency-change processes are customer operational responsibilities.

e2c1a3b4-3000-4000-8000-000000000030.description: Configuration is environment- and file-driven. Customer documents the change-control workflow for the deployment.

implemented-requirements.description: Administrative and project permissions restrict application-level changes. Repository, deployment pipeline, host, secret-store, and production configuration access are controlled by the customer.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Application-level administrative and project permissions restrict who can change configuration and project data.

implemented-requirements.description: PAPYRUS_PROFILE gates authentication, model endpoint, internet use, agent availability, and cross-domain features. Customers set secure values and validate them against the authorized environment.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: PAPYRUS_PROFILE enforces configuration defaults that constrain authentication, model endpoints, internet use, agents, and export per profile.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus can disable agents, external model endpoints, internet-assisted discovery, and cross-domain export by profile. Customers remove unused services, block unnecessary ports, and constrain runtime capabilities.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: By profile, Papyrus disables agents, external model endpoints, internet discovery, and cross-domain export where not permitted.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus publishes a lockfile and can produce SPDX or CycloneDX SBOMs for application dependencies. Customers add operating system, container, hardware, IdP, database, model server, and infrastructure components.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: The repository publishes a pnpm lockfile and CycloneDX/SPDX SBOMs for application dependencies.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus supports explicit service binding, profile-based internet restrictions, authenticated project-scoped WebSocket sessions, and no required public discovery or relay infrastructure. Firewalls, proxies, segmentation, CDS boundaries, and enclave routing remain customer controls.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: The service is bound to a deployment-specific address with authenticated WebSocket sessions and no required public discovery or relay.

implemented-requirements.description: Browser, API, and realtime WebSocket traffic can use TLS through the authoritative Papyrus service. Customers provision certificates, approved cipher policy, termination architecture, and any required FIPS-validated modules.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: REST and WebSocket traffic can use TLS through the authoritative Papyrus service.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus uses a deployment identity for session and transfer signing, TLS certificates, SAML certificates, OIDC verification keys, trusted deployment identities, and a pinned license authority key. Customers define key custody, approved generation, backup, rotation, revocation, escrow, and destruction.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: The service uses a deployment identity for signing, validates pinned license keys, and uses OIDC/SAML/TLS trust material. Customer manages custody, rotation, and destruction.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus relies on platform cryptographic implementations for TLS, WebAuthn, X.509, token signatures, signed licenses, and QUIC. Algorithm availability does not itself establish FIPS validation; customers select validated modules when required.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Platform crypto is used for TLS, WebAuthn, X.509, token signing, and license validation. FIPS-validated module selection is the customer's responsibility.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus binds requests to validated session tokens, protects state-changing browser flows with CSRF challenges, validates WebAuthn challenges, and validates OIDC state and PKCE data.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Requests are bound to validated session tokens; CSRF challenges protect state-changing flows; WebAuthn challenges and OIDC state/PKCE are validated.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus stores projects, credentials, audit records, and configuration locally. Encryption at rest is inherited from customer-managed full-disk, volume, database, or platform encryption and associated key management.

e2c1a3b4-3003-4000-8000-000000000033.description: Encryption at rest is inherited from customer-managed full-disk/volume/database encryption.

implemented-requirements.description: Beag Labs tracks application and dependency defects, publishes updated releases, and maintains lockfile changes. Customers define patch windows, test updates, deploy remediations, and document risk acceptance.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Beag Labs tracks defects and publishes patched releases with lockfile updates. Customer defines patch windows and risk acceptance.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus exposes audit, authentication, collaboration-session, agent, transfer, and integrity events suitable for operational monitoring. Customers collect, retain, correlate, alert on, and respond to those events in their monitoring platform.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: The service emits audit, auth, session, agent, transfer, and integrity events for monitoring. Customer collects and correlates in their SIEM.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus supports deterministic dependency resolution, signed-license validation, bundle verification, and hash-linked audit verification. Customers verify release provenance, hashes or signatures, container provenance, and deployment integrity.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Deterministic dependency resolution, signed-license validation, bundle verification, and hash-linked audit verification are supported.

implemented-requirements.description: The daemon validates authentication responses, request bodies, project permissions, cross-domain bundles, node types, and security-sensitive configuration before processing.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Auth responses, request bodies, permissions, cross-domain bundles, node types, and config are validated before processing.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus returns bounded error responses and avoids intentionally exposing private keys, tokens, or internal credential material. Customers configure production logging and reverse proxies to prevent diagnostic leakage.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Error responses are bounded and avoid exposing keys, tokens, or credential material.

implemented-requirements.description: Beag Labs performs source, dependency, license, and SBOM analysis and remediates supported product vulnerabilities. Customers scan deployed hosts, containers, infrastructure, model servers, and customer integrations.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Beag Labs performs source/dependency/license/SBOM analysis. Customer scans deployed infrastructure.

implemented-requirements.description: The repository includes type checking, linting, unit tests, daemon tests, authentication verification paths, and dependency review. Release evidence should record executed checks and known exceptions.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Type checking, linting, unit tests, daemon tests, auth verification, and dependency review are in the repository.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus records dependency versions in pnpm lockfiles and is designed to publish SBOMs and release hashes. Beag Labs maintains source-to-release traceability; customers preserve artifacts and verify them during intake and deployment.

65d5f633-63f1-48cf-a13e-7e75e991d882.description: Dependency versions are in lockfiles; SBOMs and release hashes are produced. Customer verifies at intake.
